pattern.crimePattern: payroll manager stealing pension deductions kills the staff welfare representative who found out
pattern.notes: Fictional resort. Unremitted pension deductions and ghost employees are documented abuses; the case never implies a real pension fund is at fault: the money never reached any fund.

ob.reportedBy: Night security supervisor, Coral Tide Resort, Mtwapa
ob.text: The night security supervisor of Coral Tide Resort, Mtwapa, reports that housekeeper Riziki Chai (29), the staff's elected welfare representative, was found dead in the staff-quarters laundry at 23:50.

people.name: Riziki Chai
people.bio: Elected by the staff to speak for them. Asked for everyone's pension statements last month.

image.brief: Mijikenda Kenyan young woman, late 20s, a housekeeping uniform with a name badge, hair in neat cornrows, a folder held against her chest, determined, ID-photo framing

people.name: Catherine Kathure
people.bio: Runs payroll for 140 staff. Lives in Nyali. Known to the staff as "Mama Catherine HR".

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 50s, a tailored skirt suit, a staff lanyard, short relaxed hair, a large designer-style handbag, gracious smile, ID-photo framing

people.name: Anthony Gikonyo
people.bio: Accused Riziki of stealing his watch that morning and shouted at her at reception.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 40s, a linen beach shirt, a bare pale band on his wrist where a watch usually sits, red-faced and embarrassed, ID-photo framing

people.name: Kache Mwaro
people.bio: Shares a room with Riziki in the staff quarters. They argued about money.

image.brief: Mijikenda Kenyan young woman, mid 20s, a kitchen hairnet and white chef's jacket, eyes swollen from crying, ID-photo framing

people.name: Jumaa Tsuma
people.bio: Guards the staff gate and keeps its book.

people.name: Neema Chai
people.bio: Lives in Kilifi. Received Riziki's last message.

facts.text: Housekeeper Riziki Chai, the staff's welfare representative, was found dead in the staff-quarters laundry at 23:50.
Riziki was struck with the laundry's steam press iron.
Riziki's phone: an incoming call at 22:41 from the contact 'Mama Catherine HR', 40 seconds.
WhatsApp to her sister at 22:45: 'Naenda kukutana na HR laundry. Nimeshika ushahidi wa pension.' (Going to meet HR at the laundry. I've got the pension evidence.)
Neema: last week Riziki told her the staff pension contributions "for everyone" had not been paid in for two years.
Neema is in Kilifi; she received the message there and called the hotel at 23:30.
An empty folder in Riziki's locker: 'Pension — staff statements'.
Staff gate book: 'C. Kathure — out 18:05', then 'C. Kathure — in 22:30 — out 23:22'.
Jumaa: at about 22:50 he saw Catherine walk from the admin block towards the quarters "with her handbag, at night, which she never does".
Jumaa: Riziki's roommate Kache Mwaro is on the kitchen night shift. They argued about money last week.
Jumaa: "Some people say HR was jealous when the staff chose Riziki."
Jumaa was at the staff gate all night; his own clock-in book shows his rounds every half hour.
PesaPap: for 24 months, a monthly 'salary — Mwaka Kenga' from the hotel payroll account has landed on Catherine's own registered number.
Records, Catherine's number: call to Riziki at 22:41; Mtwapa mast 22:25–23:30.
Staff list: no employee called Mwaka Kenga exists in any department. Riziki is a housekeeper; Catherine is the HR manager.
Duty manager: that morning the guest Anthony Gikonyo accused Riziki of stealing his watch and shouted at her at reception.
Duty manager: the watch was found in Mr Gikonyo's own room safe at 20:00. He left an apology note for Riziki at reception.
Bar till: Anthony Gikonyo's tab, orders at 22:30, 22:55, 23:20 and 23:45.
Kitchen clock card: K. Mwaro in 18:00, out 02:00. The head chef says she didn't leave the pass all night.
Riziki's payslips: overtime paid every month.
Flyer on the staff board: 'Ardhi ya ufukweni inauzwa — beachfront plots, Mtwapa & Kilifi. Mvua Holdings. Till 880 214.'
Catherine: "I left the hotel at six and was home in Nyali all evening."
Catherine: "Riziki was a good girl. Very emotional."
Catherine: "I came back to finish payroll. I never went near the quarters."
Anthony: "I was at the bar all night. I owe that girl an apology."
Kache: "I was in the kitchen until two."
Kache: Riziki lent her money for her mother's hospital bill. They argued about when she'd pay it back, "but she said don't worry".

interrogations.intro: Catherine arrives from Nyali in the morning, immaculate. "Riziki? I can't believe it. Such a good girl."

topics.reply: Pension statements? The staff can ask for those any time. Nothing to hide.
That guest shouted at her in front of everybody yesterday morning. About a watch.

interrogations.intro: Anthony is at the bar again, drinking coffee this time. "I accused her of stealing my watch. It was in my own safe. I owe that girl an apology."
Kache stands at the kitchen pass with her hands flat on the steel. "I can't talk. I have orders."

topics.reply: She lent me money for my mother's hospital bill. We argued about when I'd pay. She said don't worry. She always said don't worry.

interrogations.intro: Neema, on video from Kilifi, can't stop shaking her head. "She said she was going to fix it. For everybody."

topics.reply: Mama Catherine HR. Riziki said she was the one who signs everything.

interrogations.intro: Jumaa runs his finger down tonight's page. "Managers sign too. Everyone signs at my gate."

topics.reply: Madam HR came back at half past ten. At ten to eleven she walked to the quarters with her handbag. At night. She never does that.

contradictions.reaction: I came back to finish payroll. It's the end of the month. I was in my office. I never went near the quarters.

words.text: Riziki was about to expose the stolen pension contributions

prosecutor.pass: A call at 22:41, the gate book, and the guard who saw her walk to the quarters. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. The loud guest was at the bar all night apologising. Who called her to the laundry?
No. Read the gate book. Managers sign too.

prosecutor.pass: A ghost on the payroll for two years, and a welfare rep with the statements. Clean.
fail: She did it. But not over a watch or a loan. What was in that empty folder?
Read the staff list. Who is Mwaka Kenga?

proof.concludes: Catherine called Riziki at 22:41. Riziki went to meet "HR" at the laundry carrying the pension evidence. The evidence is gone.
Catherine wasn't home. She signed back in at 22:30, walked to the quarters at 22:50 and signed out at 23:22.
For two years a "Mwaka Kenga" salary has gone to Catherine's own number, and there is no Mwaka Kenga on the staff. The pension evidence would have exposed her. Catherine Kathure killed Riziki.

eliminations.why: Anthony was ordering at the bar at 22:30, 22:55, 23:20 and 23:45.
Kache was on the kitchen pass from 18:00 to 02:00.
Jumaa was at the staff gate all night, his rounds logged every half hour.
The watch was in the guest's own safe, and that was his accusation, not Catherine's.
The loan was between Riziki and Kache, and Kache was in the kitchen.
Riziki's overtime was paid every month.
Riziki was a housekeeper and Catherine a manager. The welfare post isn't a job Catherine could hold.

reconstruction.text: For two years Catherine deducts pension contributions from every payslip and pays them in nowhere. A ghost employee, "Mwaka Kenga", draws a salary into her own number.
Riziki, the staff's welfare rep, asks for the official pension statements. Two years of zeros.
22:41. "Mama Catherine HR" calls: let's meet privately, before you embarrass the hotel. 22:45: Riziki tells her sister she's going, with the evidence.
About 23:00, in the laundry, Catherine reaches for the statements. Riziki won't let go. The steam iron.
23:22. Catherine signs out at the staff gate with her handbag. The folder in Riziki's locker is empty.

tier1.line: Who called her at 22:41, and where did she say she was going?

tier2.line: She says home in Nyali from six. The staff gate keeps a book, and managers sign it too.

tier1.line: Read the staff list carefully. Then ask for her records.

tier2.line: A monthly salary for a man who doesn't exist, landing on her number.

glossary.def: Mother; also a respectful way to address or name a woman.
Fictional mobile-money service used in the game.

ui.beatNotes: Records that prove WHY, not WHO: the first case where the records request is decisive for the motive more than the location. The notebook's WHY panel lights up when a fact connects to a motive word.
